mathgap.title: Signed 'has more than' interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form "X has more than Y" (including "X has N more than Y") as a signed difference X − Y = N (or X = Y + N), preserving the order of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement compares two quantities using "has more than" or "has N more than".
mathgap.example: Treating "Alice has more than Bob" as |Alice − Bob| = N (absolute difference) instead of the signed difference Alice − Bob = N.

mathgap.title: Model transfers as net changes
mathgap.principle: When a transfer "X gives N to Y" occurs, subtract N from X and add N to Y, updating each person's count accordingly.
mathgap.example: Adding N to both X and Y instead of subtracting from X and adding to Y.

mathgap.title: Systematic equation solving
mathgap.principle: Introduce a distinct variable for each person and translate every relevant statement into a linear equation, building a complete system before solving.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After parsing all statements, before attempting to solve.
mathgap.example: Omitting a variable for a person who appears only in a relational statement, causing missing constraints.

mathgap.title: Signed difference phrasing
mathgap.principle: Interpret "difference between X and Y" as the signed difference X − Y, preserving the order as presented in the statement.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement refers to the "difference between" two quantities.
mathgap.example: Reading "difference between A and B" as |A − B| (absolute) or as B − A, reversing the intended order.

mathgap.title: Include transfers as constraints before solving relational equations
mathgap.principle: Apply all transfer statements first, updating each person's count, and then translate relational equations using those updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Immediately after handling all transfers, before processing any difference or "has more than" equations.
mathgap.example: Solving relational equations with pre‑transfer counts, leading to an inconsistent system.

mathgap.title: Direct counts as initial constraints
mathgap.principle: Treat statements that give an explicit count (e.g., "X has N items") as the initial amount before any transfers or other changes.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a direct count statement.
mathgap.example: Assuming a direct count is the final amount after transfers, thereby ignoring subsequent transfer effects.

mathgap.title: Answer formatting
mathgap.principle: Output the final answer using the exact required format: "The final answer is \boxed{<integer>}".
mathgap.when_to_apply: When producing the final answer for the problem.
mathgap.example: Writing "The answer is 24" or omitting the LaTeX box, causing the verifier to reject the response.

mathgap.title: Complete system solving
mathgap.principle: After translating all constraints into linear equations, actually solve the system (or directly isolate the target variable) to obtain the numeric answer.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Once the full set of equations has been assembled.
mathgap.example: Guessing a value for the target variable without solving the equations, leading to an incorrect answer.

mathgap.title: Aggregate multiple transfers per person
mathgap.principle: Sum all incoming and outgoing transfer amounts for each person to obtain a net change, then apply that net change to the person's count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a person appears in more than one transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Applying each transfer sequentially without aggregating, which can double‑count or miss some transfers.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y", first evaluate X's current count after any prior transfers; if the condition holds, set X's count to 0 and add its count to Y, otherwise make no change.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a conditional transfer (an "if" statement) appears in the problem.
mathgap.example: Assuming the transfer always occurs regardless of whether the condition is satisfied, resulting in incorrect final counts.

mathgap.description: Treating direct count statements as final counts after transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the given explicit count already reflects all later changes, ignoring subsequent transfer statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret direct counts as initial amounts, then apply all transfers before using those numbers in relational equations.

mathgap.description: Applying transfers in the wrong direction
mathgap.why_it_happens: Confusion between giver and receiver leads to adding to the giver and subtracting from the receiver.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "X gives N to Y" means X loses N and Y gains N; update counts accordingly.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase "difference between A and B" is read as |A − B|, losing the sign and order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order given in the statement: treat it as the signed difference A − B.

mathgap.description: Applying relational equations before applying transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model translates and solves equations using pre‑transfer counts, violating the problem's chronology.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: First process all transfer statements, update counts, then translate relational equations using the updated values.

mathgap.description: Incomplete solving: failing to derive the answer from the constraints, leading to a guess
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model stops after setting up some equations without fully solving the system, then guesses a value for the target variable.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: After building the full system, solve it completely (or isolate the target variable) before producing the answer.
